blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
High-stakes negotiations with British partners reward two qualities above all: patience and the ability to keep the room comfortable. The British do not like negotiations that feel forced, adversarial or theatrical. They prefer a careful, almost reflective conversation where both sides feel they are thinking together rather than fighting.

That does not mean weakness. Experienced British negotiators can be very firm indeed — but the firmness is wrapped in courtesy, and it is revealed slowly, through what they decline to agree to rather than through raised voices. A quiet "I'm not sure we'd be able to go there" may be a final no. Mistake it for an opening for further pressure, and you will lose the relationship that would have made the next three deals possible.

The senior negotiator's most valuable skill is knowing when to stop pushing. In British rooms, the moment of stopping is often the moment of winning. The partner feels that they have been heard and respected, that you understand the limits, and that a deal with you is one they can live with — which is, in the end, the only kind of deal worth having.

items.q: According to the text, which two qualities do negotiations with British partners reward above all?
options: Patience and keeping the room comfortable
items.why: "reward two qualities above all: patience and the ability to keep the room comfortable."

items.q: How is British firmness typically revealed, according to the text?
options: Slowly, through what they decline to agree to
items.why: "revealed slowly, through what they decline to agree to rather than through raised voices."

items.q: A quiet "I'm not sure we'd be able to go there" is best understood as…
options: a sign of uncertainty to be exploited
an invitation to negotiate the price
items.why: "A quiet 'I'm not sure we'd be able to go there' may be a final no."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Knowing when to stop pushing is a senior skill.
Courtesy and firmness can coexist in a negotiator.
When a British partner softens the language, it is your cue to press harder.
The relationship can matter more than a single deal.
items.why: Inferência: o texto avisa que confundir a cortesia com uma brecha para pressão custa o relacionamento — o autor discordaria disso.

items.q: What does "the moment of stopping is often the moment of winning" suggest?
options: Winning depends mainly on speaking last
Restraint can secure the deal that pressure would destroy
items.why: Inferência: parar de pressionar no momento certo faz o parceiro se sentir respeitado — e é isso que fecha o acordo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver aconselhando um colega no meio da negociação. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, before you go back in this afternoon, let me tell you what I think is actually happening. They've gone quiet since yesterday, and you're reading that as hesitation. I'd read it very differently.

When their lead said "we might have considered a longer term earlier in the process", that wasn't nostalgia. That was a door closing, politely. Hypothetical past, past its moment — he was telling you the term is settled and he'd rather you didn't reopen it.

So my advice is: don't push this afternoon. If you go in and press for another two points on the fee, you'll get a very courteous refusal, and every courteous refusal after that gets a little colder. These people don't slam doors; they simply stop opening new ones.

What I'd do is thank them for the flexibility they've already shown, restate the two things you genuinely can't move on, and then leave a silence. Let them fill it. If they come back with a small concession, you're nearly there. If they don't, you have your answer, and you've kept the relationship — which, with this firm, is worth more than the last half a point.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How is the colleague currently interpreting the counterparty's silence?
items.why: "you're reading that as hesitation. I'd read it very differently."

items.q: What does Oliver say "we might have considered a longer term earlier in the process" really meant?
options: A request for a longer term now
An invitation to renegotiate the term
items.why: "That was a door closing, politely… he was telling you the term is settled."

items.q: What does Oliver advise the colleague to do this afternoon?
options: Bring in a more senior negotiator
Not push, and leave a silence for them to fill
Press for two more points on the fee
items.why: "don't push this afternoon… restate the two things you genuinely can't move on, and then leave a silence."

items.q: What does Oliver mean by "They don't slam doors; they simply stop opening new ones"?
options: They will end the meeting abruptly
They prefer to negotiate by email
Their refusal is gradual and quiet, not dramatic
They rarely put anything in writing
items.why: Inferência: a recusa britânica não é ruidosa — vai esfriando aos poucos, fechando oportunidades sem confronto.

items.q: What does Oliver value most in dealing with this firm?
options: Closing the deal as fast as possible
Winning the last half a point on the fee
items.why: Inferência: ele diz que o relacionamento vale mais que o último meio ponto — a relação é a prioridade.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "This was a high-stakes negotiation, with the whole partnership on the line." High-stakes means…
options: involving very serious risk or consequences
held at a senior level only
items.why: High-stakes = de alto risco, em que muito está em jogo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "He kept the tone warm and ___ , never letting the talks feel like a fight."
items.why: Reflective = reflexivo: a conversa ponderada que os britânicos preferem.

items.q: "Her firmness was never loud, but the answer was clearly no." Firmness here means…
items.why: Firmness = firmeza: manter a posição com convicção, sem gritar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "They chose to ___ the offer rather than reject it bluntly."
items.why: To decline = recusar, de forma educada.

items.q: "It was a deal both sides could live with." To live with something means to…
options: accept it and be able to work under it
items.why: To live with = conviver com, aceitar como algo com que se pode trabalhar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em negociações de alto nível. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Their board still has to sign off on the revised terms." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "The partner pushed back on the exclusivity clause." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed the outline, but nobody followed through on the detail." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Shaving half a point off the fee won't move the needle for them." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Let's not read too much into their silence." This means we should not…
options: interpret it as carrying more meaning than it does
items.why: Read too much into = atribuir mais significado do que algo realmente tem.
